transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15 14:30 PDT | Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Ava Nguyen (CS), Elena Morales (Borealis), Darius Kowalski (CTO), Sana Iqbal (Security), Tom Becker (Procurement)

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to keep this as a short checkpoint. Quick agenda — cap bump, eu private plan, paperwork.
[00:25] Elena Morales: Sounds good, thanks Priya. We're short on time so maybe quick rundowns then dive where needed.
[01:05] Marcus Li: Quick context from engineering side — we looked at the telemetry from your prod traffic, peak concurrent tokens are up about 2.4x QoQ which is why you asked about moving from the 2 GPU pool to 4. We also ran a sim of the batching profile and saw latency holds around 120-160ms p50 on the dedicated config.
[02:30] Darius Kowalski: Right, and our threshold for UX is p95 under 400ms for web flows, and less than 700ms for async backfills. So that 4x sounds sensible, what I want to understand is the burst behaviour — if sudden traffic spikes hit, how quickly does Redwood spin up extra capacity?
[03:15] Marcus Li: Good q. For Dedicated we do reserved pods plus burst capacity — typically warm scaling in 30-90s depending on quota and GPU type. For guaranteed sub-100ms we can recommend pre-warm policies and warm standbys, tradeoff is cost.
[03:50] Elena Morales: Can you quantify cost for keeping a warm standby vs pure burst?
[04:05] Priya Shah: We'll provide two line items in the quote — reserved + warm standby (costed as 50% of a reserved pool) vs pure burst per-minute billing. I'll put those numbers in the updated quote.
[04:22] Tom Becker: From procurement perspective we need annual spend estimates and PO format — can you send that in a consolidated spreadsheet?
[04:35] Priya Shah: Yes, Tom I'll attach a spend forecast and PO template.
[05:10] Sana Iqbal: On the EU private deployment — our compliance team requires data not leave EU. We want to know if Redwood Private can run in our Frankfurt VPC and what the control plane visibility looks like. Also KMS — we need customer-managed keys.
[05:45] Marcus Li: Correct, the Private option supports a customer VPC with private control plane. We support customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM). For Frankfurt region we have validated images and distro but need to run the collector for metrics behind their network. There's a couple of installers — one for air-gapped on-prem and one for VPC.
[06:30] Elena Morales: Air-gapped would be ideal for a subset of workloads — like underwriting models — but maybe overkill for non-sensitive. We want a hybrid: private plane in eu-central and an on-prem connector for a handful of sensitive calls.
[07:02] Marcus Li: That's a common hybrid pattern. Pilot can use private control plane + on-prem connector for a limited model set. We'll document the network ports, cert rotation, and monitoring hooks.
[07:35] Darius Kowalski: Any changes to latency for those on-prem connectors? The underwriting flow needs consistent <200ms.
[08:00] Marcus Li: On-prem connector will add the network hop; if the models are hosted in the customer's on-prem hardware you'd see local latency similar to local infra. If models remain in Redwood's Frankfurt pool but connector proxies calls, expect additional 20-80ms depending on routing.
[08:45] Sana Iqbal: We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and log retention for 3 years — is that possible?
[09:05] Ava Nguyen: Yes we can ship structured logs to your SIEM (S3/Cloudwatch/Elastic) and discuss retention; long retention is an add-on commercial item but technically supported. I'll include retention options in the follow-up.
[09:32] Priya Shah: On contract timing, you mentioned renewal is late Oct?
[09:40] Elena Morales: Yes renewal window opens Oct 26; procurement usually needs two weeks to approve a renew/upgrade. So aiming to have final commercial terms by Oct 12 would be ideal.
[10:05] Priya Shah: Great — that aligns. We'll target the quote by Sep 17 to give you time.
[11:20] Tom Becker: On the PO we also need to ensure milestone invoicing — is Redwood ok with quarterly invoicing on committed capacity?
[11:35] Priya Shah: Quarterly invoicing is fine; we'll mirror the committed capacity in the SOW and add an appendix for burst charges.
[12:10] Darius Kowalski: I want to bring up model quantization and perf tradeoffs — our ML team asks whether Redwood will manage quantized model artifacts or do we push quantized versions?
[12:45] Marcus Li: We can host both FP16 and int8 variants. For production we recommend testing int8 with our Optimize tooling; Redwood can host the quantized artifact if you provide it, or we can run quantization and validate for you under a tooling engagement.
[13:30] Elena Morales: Are there any licensing constraints if we bring our own model weights?
[13:50] Priya Shah: We'll put a BYOM (bring your own model) clause in the SOW that covers IP ownership and ensures compliance with any third-party licenses.
[14:20] [transcription glitch] Speaker 4: ...uh the — the thing about uh the, uh..
[14:40] Marcus Li: Sorry, that was me saying that we'll need to validate checkpoints and run a short regen test to ensure perf stability.
[15:10] Sana Iqbal: For keys — are you managing key rotation or do we? Because our policy forces rotation every 30 days.
[15:30] Marcus Li: Customer-managed KMS means you control rotation; Redwood can integrate with KMS APIs so the runtime reads keys but doesn't store plaintext. We'll also publish audit logs showing key usage.
[16:05] Elena Morales: Good. Can you confirm SOC2 scope? We need to know if the hosted control plane is covered or only Private packages.
[16:25] Ava Nguyen: Redwood's hosted API is SOC2 compliant; for Private deployments we provide the attestation of the Redwood control plane components, but some responsibilities shift to the customer in a self-managed deployment — we'll provide a shared responsibility matrix.
[17:05] Darius Kowalski: Competitors popped in earlier — Anthropic did a quick outreach offering to host in eu-west their managed stack, but they don't support on-prem connector which is a blocker.
[17:30] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll emphasize the hybrid approach in the docs.
[18:40] Elena Morales: Ok pilot scoping — what does Redwood recommend as success criteria?
[19:05] Marcus Li: Recommend pilot run with 1 model (underwriting), run for 2 weeks at production qps ~20% of current, measure: p95 latency, error rate, per-token cost, and functional correctness (regressions). If that passes we ramp to full fleet.
[19:45] Darius Kowalski: Makes sense. We also want to test failover — if Frankfurt capacity is constrained, can Redwood route to other EU region or fallback to lower-cost model?
[20:12] Marcus Li: Yes, we support routing policies: failover to another region or to a smaller, compatible model. We'll document compatible fallback models and the expected quality differential.
[21:00] Priya Shah: Quick pause — any blockers on your side for the Sep 17 quote?
[21:12] Tom Becker: Need procurement template; also need clarity on termination clauses for the added capacity.
[21:30] Priya Shah: We'll add termination and change control language for capacity adjustments.
[22:05] Elena Morales: One last machine learning question — will Redwood provide automatic KV cache warming or do we handle warm-up?
[22:30] Marcus Li: We have prefix/KV caching features and can preload popular prefixes during pilot. We'll provide a caching plan and warm-up scripts.
[23:20] [short silence; multiple speakers muting/unmuting]
[24:00] Sana Iqbal: On security checklist — can you send the network diagram, KMS integration notes, and the SOC2 report?
[24:25] Ava Nguyen: Yes, I'll share the documents. Some parts (SOC2) are redacted; we'll also provide contact for our security team to do a deeper review.
[25:10] Darius Kowalski: For the EU private package — any special hardware requirements? We prefer A10x or A100-NVMe preference?
[25:38] Marcus Li: We validated on A100 and H100 families; for cost/perf we can recommend A10x for mixed workloads but underwriting large sequences — H100 or A100 may be better. We'll include recommendations.
[26:05] Priya Shah: OK team, recap — Marcus will produce network diagram + on-prem checklist; Ava will send SOC2 and retention options; I will send the updated quote with warm standby and burst options by Sep 17. Tom will share procurement timeline. Sana will send compliance must-haves and Darius will confirm pilot model.
[26:45] Elena Morales: Perfect. Any other questions?
[27:00] Tom Becker: One small ask — can invoices be made to Borealis Holdings LLC and include MSA reference?
[27:12] Priya Shah: Yes we can. We'll include MSA reference in the quote.
[28:00] [closing pleasantries]
[28:10] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and set the pilot kickoff next week if timelines hold.
[28:25] Elena Morales: Thanks, talk soon.
[28:30] [call ended — auto transcript continues garbled text for a few sec]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional word swaps and truncations; multiple short interruptions and audio overlaps recorded around 00:14–00:28 and 24:00–24:30.
